correctness.rationale: With k selected candidates there are 2k incidences; each adjacent selected pair corresponds to one twice-represented voter and subtracts 1/2 from that incidence total. Thus swaps strictly improve the score precisely when they reduce the selected adjacency count a (equivalently increase the number of one-runs). Removing the middle of a triple removes two adjacencies; if it cannot be swapped profitably, all zeros must have two selected neighbors, which with the specified counts forces alternation. At a nonoptimal local maximum only singleton and double-one runs remain. A zero with no selected neighbors gives an improvement by swapping out one member of a double. The patterns 1100, 0011, and boundary 011 or 110 also give explicit improving moves by moving the one beside the relevant gap into the adjacent zero. It follows that the a extra zeros, after paying one zero per interior gap, are either second zeros between two singleton runs or a boundary zero next to a singleton. A block of t singleton runs can pay for at most t extra zeros, because at least one double-one run exists and the block cannot touch both ends. Therefore a≤s where k=2a+s, yielding a≤floor(k/3). The displayed sharp word has exactly floor(k/3) doubles and only singleton-supported extra zeros. Deleting a singleton loses one run; deleting from a double leaves the run count unchanged but leaves every originally zero position adjacent to some remaining one. No swap can increase the number of runs. Alternation gives the global value and is forced at a=0. The k=3 word is a witness, not a uniqueness statement (its reflection also works). The package's finite checker was inspected rather than run; the all-k proof does not rely on it.

evidence: The shared constant is sharp for half-size greedy committees on cycles of size divisible by six, whereas the frozen guarantee quantifies over every path swap-local committee. The general one-swap theorem quantifies over the correct move but lacks the restricted extremal profile.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Closing the voter path changes the interval incidence and availability of a swap; for instance adjoining an unselected closing edge to the k=3 witness allows a cycle swap that removes the adjacency at the initial double. Sequential tie resolutions are also not a statement about every exchange-stable committee. The previously inspected claims thus do not supply the no-improving-swap upper bound on a or its matching path witnesses.

value.rationale: Even the canonical path of two-person supports has suboptimal local maxima, although its global optimum is immediate. The exact floor correction gives the first obstruction and a sharp quantitative guarantee for every size; the singleton-run charging proof identifies why the loss is limited. This separates the performance of fixed-size local exchange from tractability of global optimization on a natural restricted election domain.
